title: Engagements, Ralph Foster and Mike DeLay at the Lavida dance hall
summary: Lists hotel and boat engagements around 1927, then playing with Ralph Foster and Mike DeLay at the Lavida on Iberville until 1934, describing the hall and its bandstand.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Around 26, I believe, from about around 27. So, all the doing that, that next year is when I went to a dance hall. We had so many engagements during them years, back in 27. We played our chair by Jack Sheen. We played on the boat, the captain. We played at the Junk Hotel. We played at the Rosecrunk Hotel. We played at the Rosecrunk Hotel. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. booth and have a restaurant. We had been playing for so many times, all during the music, so many different engagements that we played. I believe it's all right here on T'Nan and Ramport. I believe I played dance. You know all engagements and it's a part, but I went into the dance hall and I played there kind of regular. I played there with Ralph Foster. Car said there, leading the band, and I played with him. He's a band then. Ralph Foster's band. We left there, I left there, and we come around here and I played with Mike DeLay by the LaVita. I stood there until 34. What was the LaVita? Right next to the point on I was building. We had a dance hall. That's the place I was telling you me and Pai Joe played the last dance there. We closed it up. We was playing there when the place closed up for good. Did we get the location on the tape? That's on Iberville between Maganda and Ramport. You know right where that lot is, the parking lot? Right next to that parking lot because we used to go in through the parking lot to go in the back door. You know, get right to the bandstand. The bandstand was in the back of the hall? Yeah. Was it raised? Oh yeah, the bandstand was raised. How high? About like a stage. Four feet or something like that? Yeah, about four feet I would say. We had one in the middle of the front next door. See? And laying on, the chance of the Budweiser.
That was near Ramport Street then?

The Budweiser, no. The front was near Ramport. Close to the Ramport. Close to the Ramport. That was some rough days. The Budweiser went there. The Budweiser went there in 1930.
